task_type_fields.evidence: Observed once in GitHub Actions run 32923010097: rust median 285269.89us against absolute ceiling 281973.47us, 1.2% over. The two following CI runs passed the perf-floors job. The approved CI repair plan treats it as hosted-runner variance against an anchor that already carries a documented per-anchor exemption, and explicitly says not to retune it in the CI-green repair. No local reproduction was attempted in this turn.

evidence.note: Second perf-floors anchor with the identical signature, found during epic sase-um.9.5 and proposed by phase bead sase-um.9.5.3 (note #7) on 2026-08-28. Full CI run 33226037754, perf-floors job 99030887383, SHA 1a1463028: tests/perf/phase7_check_regression.py evaluate_query_many.synthetic_1000_specs.persistent_query_keystroke reported a rust median of 193.90us against the 2.90x ceiling 193.44us — 0.46us (0.24%) over, while still beating the live Python path (~5292us) by ~27x. Every other Phase 7E, launch, view-hints, disk-load, and catalog floor passed in the same job, and the anchor passed on the following runs. Same root cause and same desired remediation as this bead: hosted-runner variance measured against a tight per-anchor absolute ceiling, where retuning the anchor would hide the noise instead of making the gate resistant to a single noisy sample. Recorded here rather than as a second bead because a fix that only moves the scan_facade ceiling would leave this anchor red on the next noisy runner.
